findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() is dead, self-contradictory logic
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the inverted sense: `enabled` is true when the flag is *off*) and then returns `false` from both branches, so the feature-flag lookup has no effect at all. The intent (always disable SQL expressions) is achieved only by accident of the final `return false`. This is a trap for the next maintainer: anyone re-enabling the feature by deleting the `if` block would end up enabling SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled, and vice versa. It should be a plain unconditional disable (or a correctly-oriented flag check) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264.

findings.title: Error message does not explain that the feature was intentionally removed
findings.body: Returning `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` for `QueryTypeSQL` is misleading for operators who have explicitly enabled the still-registered `sqlExpressions` feature toggle: it reads like a missing implementation rather than a deliberate security-driven disable. Users will have no indication why their previously working queries fail. Mention that SQL expressions are disabled in this build/version (and consider removing or marking the feature toggle as non-functional so the documented toggle doesn't advertise a capability that no longer exists).

findings.title: Legacy SQL command path now fails with an opaque 'error reading SQL command'
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` still calls `sql.TablesList`, which now unconditionally fails because `DB.RunCommands` returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. The caller converts this into `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql")` with public message "error reading SQL command", so any existing panel or alert rule using a SQL expression (through `UnmarshalSQLCommand`, the non-reader path) breaks with a message suggesting the user's SQL is malformed rather than that the feature has been disabled. It also logs the full raw SQL at Warn level on every such request. Prefer short-circuiting with an explicit "SQL expressions are disabled" error.

findings.title: NoData result is immediately overwritten by TableData
findings.body: In `Execute`, when `frame.Rows() == 0` the code sets `rsp.Values = mathexp.Values{mathexp.NoData{Frame: frame}}` but the following statement unconditionally reassigns `rsp.Values = mathexp.Values{mathexp.TableData{Frame: frame}}`, so the NoData branch can never take effect and empty results are always reported as an empty table. The second assignment needs to be in an `else` branch. (Pre-existing, but this file is being touched and the dead branch will mislead future readers.)

findings.title: DB.TablesList stub is unused dead code
findings.body: `DB.TablesList` is never called: `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` uses the package-level `TablesList` function, which goes through `DB.RunCommands`. Keeping an unused method on the stub type adds confusion about which entry point actually gates SQL execution; either remove it or make the package-level function delegate to it.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This change is a security fix (CVE-2024-9264) whose entire effect is that `QueryTypeSQL` queries must be rejected and that `sql.DB` never executes anything. There is no test covering `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `type: sql` returning an error (with the feature toggle both on and off), nor one covering `NewSQLCommand`/`sql.TablesList` failing. Without such a test, a future refactor of `enableSqlExpressions` or re-introduction of a real `DB` implementation can silently reopen the RCE/LFI path.
